Subject: Questions on notice cutoff + TFC language (MSA redline)

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for sending the MSA + order form last week. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed and attached a counter-redline (BlueHaven_MSA_counter_redline_v2.pdf). Two items we want to make sure are aligned before we sign:

1) Notice cutoff / blackout window: procurement wants a firm 60-day cutoff before renewal where contract changes or termination notices must be delivered. They want clarity about when the notice window starts (calendar day vs. business day) and whether a DocuSign signature date counts as the notice trigger.

2) Termination for convenience (TFC): we asked for limited liability in the event of early termination and a 30-day service wind-down commitment. We also flagged a short transition credit to cover data exports.

Can your team confirm whether Redwood can accept calendar days for the notice window and whether we can get a binding wind-down SLA (30 days) in the order form, plus a modest termination credit tied to unused committed capacity?

We are aiming to finalize by 9/15 to align with our procurement cycle. Let me know if you prefer a quick call.

Thanks —
Priyanka Shah
Director, Strategic Procurement
BlueHaven Health

Hi Priyanka —

Appreciate the clear callouts and the quick turnaround from your team. I reviewed the counter-redline and looped in Marissa (sales lead) and Laura (CS) so we can coordinate commercial and operational commitments. High level:

- Notice window: Redwood is comfortable using calendar days. We typically measure from receipt of a written notice delivered to the contracting emails (not the DocuSign envelope date). To be helpful we can add a short definitional sentence in the order form that says "Notice is effective on the date the contracting representative receives written notice via email or confirmed execution in DocuSign." This keeps both sides covered.

- TFC / wind-down: We can agree to a 30-day wind-down SLA for active customer instances and a transition assistance package. For the termination credit, we can offer a pro-rated refund of pre-paid, unused dedicated capacity (not usage-based hosted charges).

I'll ask Legal to propose specific redline text for the MSA and draft a short addendum to the order form that captures both the notice trigger language and the termination credit formula. Can your procurement team share the preferred cutoff time (e.g., 11:59pm PT on day 60) or should we stick with "end of day" local to BlueHaven?

If helpful I can set up a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the proposed language.

Best,

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com
To: jonas_weber@redwoodai.com, marissa_cole@redwoodai.com, laura_bennett@redwoodai.com
Date: 2026-09-02T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Notice cutoff + TFC language — proposed redlines

Team —

Draft language below that I recommend we push back to the customer. I kept it narrow and operational to avoid rolling TFC into broader indemnity/exposure issues: 

1) Notice window (Order Form addendum) — suggest: 
"Notice Period and Trigger: The renewal notice period shall be sixty (60) calendar days. Notice shall be effective upon Redwood's receipt of a written communication sent to contracts@redwoodai.com or upon the date of confirmed electronic execution (DocuSign) by an authorized signatory of the customer. For clarity, 'calendar days' includes weekends and public holidays. If notice is received after 11:59 PM PT on the final day of the notice period, the notice shall be deemed received on the following calendar day.

2) Termination for Convenience (MSA) — suggest: 
"Termination For Convenience: Either party may terminate the Order Form for convenience upon providing sixty (60) calendar days' written notice. Upon termination for convenience by the customer, Redwood will provide thirty (30) calendar days of wind-down support, reasonable assistance with data export, and a pro-rated credit for any pre-paid Dedicated Capacity fees for the remainder of the billing period, calculated on a daily basis. Termination by the customer shall not relieve the customer of payment for any usage incurred prior to the effective date of termination.

3) Exclusions / cap language — suggest keeping existing liability and service level sections unchanged; do not offer additional credits beyond pro-rated dedicated capacity refunds without executive approval. Any deviation (e.g., full refund or extended credits) should be escalated to Sales leadership.

If that reads well I will incorporate into the MSA redline PDF and create an order-form addendum docx for signatures. I also recommend we propose a single DocuSign envelope for both MSA and order form to avoid mismatch on effective dates.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Subject: Final proposed redlines and next steps (MSA + Order Form)

Hi Priyanka —

Thanks for the prompt review and patience while we waited on legal to weigh in. Attached are the two files: a redlined MSA incorporating the wind-down/TFC text and a short Order Form addendum that defines the 60-day calendar-day notice window and the receipt/DocuSign trigger.

Key points / tradeoffs we are proposing:
- Notice window = sixty (60) calendar days; effective on Redwood's receipt of notice or confirmed DocuSign execution. We used 11:59 PM PT as the cutoff to align internal billing cycles.
- TFC = 60-day notice; Redwood will provide a 30-day wind-down with data export support and a pro-rated refund for pre-paid Dedicated Capacity fees. This does not apply to usage-based hosted charges.
- Any request for a larger termination credit or extended wind-down beyond 30 days will require executive approval; we included an explicit escalation path in the addendum.
